title: US replaces expiring tariffs with new duties on 60 countries
gist: The US replaced its expiring 10% Section 122 global tariff with a new Section 301 duty tied to a forced-labour investigation, applying 10% or 12.5% rates across 60 trading partners (including China at 12.5%), while Brazil faces a separate 25% Section 301 tariff under a distinct case.

insights.claim: The US replaced its temporary 10% global Section 122 tariff with a new Section 301 duty tied to a forced-labour investigation, covering 60 trading partners including Canada, Mexico, India and the UK, effective 12:01am ET on 24 July 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Investors with exposure to trade flows across these 60 economies (including battery materials supply chains) should reprice tariff-driven cost assumptions now that the legal basis and rate structure have changed.
insights.quote: The US has replaced its temporary 10% global tariff with a new Section 301 duty tied to a forced-labour investigation, covering 60 trading partners including Canada, Mexico, India and the UK.
insights.locator: The US has replaced its temporary 10% global tariff

insights.claim: The prior Section 122 tariff expired because the Supreme Court had ruled the US administration could not impose duties by declaring a national emergency, forcing a shift to a Section 301 forced-labour investigation as the legal vehicle for continued tariffs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Judicial limits on emergency-powers tariffs push future US trade actions toward statutory mechanisms like Section 301, a signal for how durable and legally contestable subsequent tariff moves may be.
insights.quote: the prior Section 122 tariff – put in place after the Supreme Court ruled the administration could not impose duties by declaring a national emergency – expired.
insights.locator: The measure took effect at 12:01am ET on 24 July 2026

insights.claim: Under the new Section 301 forced-labour tariff, 14 economies with existing forced-labour import bans or relevant trade commitments get a lower 10% rate, while the remaining 46 covered economies, including China, face a 12.5% rate.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: China-linked supply chains (relevant to battery materials sourcing) remain subject to the higher 12.5% tier, sustaining cost pressure and incentives for diversification versus the 14 lower-rate economies.
insights.quote: The new rate is 10% for 14 economies with existing forced-labour import bans or relevant trade commitments, and 12.5% for the remaining 46, including China.
insights.locator: The new rate is 10% for 14 economies

insights.claim: Brazil faces a separate, higher 25% Section 301 tariff effective from 22 July 2026, imposed under a distinct case outside the 60-country forced-labour action.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Brazil-sourced goods and materials face a materially steeper tariff (25% vs 10-12.5% for the broader group), a distinct cost headwind for Brazil-linked trade and supply chains.
insights.quote: Brazil faces a separate 25% Section301 tariff from 22 July under a distinct case.
insights.locator: Brazil faces a separate 25% Section301 tariff
